security_audit.summary: All 400 presented static findings were adjudicated as false positives or expected capabilities of a JMAP mail client. The findings primarily stem from generated declarations, source maps, documentation, credential storage, protocol requests, and JavaScript syntax misclassified as process execution. No prompt injection, unauthorized credential exfiltration, or malicious persistence intent was found in the reviewed files. Static review was capped at 400/864 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 464 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Credentials and bearer tokens are stored locally for the mail session.
remediation.suggestion: Keep credential files mode 0600, avoid logging tokens, and document a secure credential rotation procedure.

remediation.issue: Authentication and JMAP endpoints can be overridden through environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before sending credentials to a custom endpoint and consider validating or allowlisting endpoint origins.

remediation.issue: JMAP requests can send messages and upload attachments.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before irreversible mail sends or attachment uploads in agent integrations.

content.user_title: Manage Atomic Mail from your AI agent
content.value_statement: Email work can require repetitive inbox checks and precise message operations. Atomic Mail gives an agent JMAP commands and presets for reading, replying to, and sending mail.
actual_capabilities: Registers an Atomic Mail inbox or connects with an existing API key.
Lists mailboxes and retrieves messages through JMAP method calls.
Sends new messages and replies with bundled JMAP presets.
Uploads attachments through the JMAP Blob extension when supported.
Resolves account and inbox values from the active Atomic Mail session.
Provides built-in help for authentication, presets, and troubleshooting.
limitations: It works only with an Atomic Mail account and compatible JMAP endpoints.
Sending, replying, and uploading attachments can make external changes.
It does not independently decide whether a message is safe or appropriate to send.
Scheduled inbox polling requires a host with native agent scheduling support.

use_cases.title: Triage a personal inbox
use_cases.description: Fetch recent messages, summarize priorities, and prepare reply options before sending.

use_cases.title: Operate a support mailbox
use_cases.description: List support messages and draft or send replies using approved JMAP operations.

use_cases.title: Build an email workflow
use_cases.description: Use JMAP presets and session variables in a controlled agent workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Check recent mail
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Atomic Mail to list my recent inbox messages. Summarize the sender, subject, and required action. Do not send anything.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a reply
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the message from [sender] about [topic]. Draft a concise reply, but ask for my approval before sending it.

prompt_templates.title: Send a confirmed message
prompt_templates.prompt: Send an email to [recipient] with subject [subject] and this approved body: [body]. Confirm the recipient and subject before sending.

prompt_templates.title: Run a JMAP operation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Atomic Mail jmap_request with [preset or operation]. Resolve only the required session variables and show a dry-run summary before any external change.

output_examples.input: List recent inbox messages and do not send mail.
output: Priority: Reply to the billing question

output_examples.input: Prepare a reply to a meeting request.
output: Draft reply: Thank you. I can join at the proposed time.

output_examples.input: Send the approved status update to the project group.
output: Message sent successfully through Atomic Mail.

best_practices: Review recipients, subject lines, and message bodies before sending.
Keep credentials in the configured private directory and never commit them.
Use bundled presets or dry runs before creating custom JMAP requests.
anti_patterns: Do not send mail based on an ambiguous request or unverified recipient.
Do not place API keys or JWTs in prompts, logs, or version control.
Do not schedule raw CLI requests without an agent workflow that reviews results.

faq.question: What account do I need?
faq.answer: You need an Atomic Mail account or a valid Atomic Mail API key.

faq.question: Can it send email?
faq.answer: Yes. It can send messages and replies through JMAP after you provide the required details.

faq.question: Can it read my inbox?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use JMAP requests to list mailboxes and retrieve messages from the configured account.

faq.question: Where are credentials stored?
faq.answer: The skill uses its configured credentials directory, which defaults to a private directory in the user home folder.

faq.question: Can it handle attachments?
faq.answer: Yes, when the configured JMAP service supports blob uploads and you provide the attachment path or data.

faq.question: Does it schedule inbox checks automatically?
faq.answer: Only hosts with native agent scheduling can run the documented polling workflow. Other hosts require manual checks or operator scheduling.
